2026Q2/005930/notes.text: Final results (nearly identical to preliminary). Revenue KRW 171.5T (+130%), operating income KRW 89.5T (+1,814%, operating margin 52.2%), net income KRW 71.3T (+1,230%). Revenue slightly missed consensus (-1.7%); operating income beat by +5.5% (per reports). ★The DS (semiconductor) division alone posted revenue of KRW 127.5T and operating income of KRW 89.2T (70% margin, 99.7% of company operating income) — record DRAM and NAND sales to AI servers. ★The DX (devices) division posted its first operating loss since the 2021 integration (-KRW 0.8T) due to rising component costs ('chipflation'). Display: revenue KRW 7.5T / operating income KRW 0.7T; Harman: revenue KRW 4.6T / operating income KRW 0.4T. A stronger dollar added KRW 3.1T to operating income; R&D a record KRW 16T. EPS KRW 10,849 (same for common and preferred shares, Samsung Newsroom). Shares spiked as much as +7.1% intraday (KRW 223,250) right after the final results but gave back all gains on worries about a semiconductor peak, closing roughly flat — the closing-basis price reaction is −0.7%. On the call, management said the memory shortage would 'persist through 2028'; an ADR listing is not under consideration.

2026Q2/AAPL/notes.text: Record June quarter. Revenue $109.4B (+16%); iPhone $54.25B (+22%) beat, while Services $30.74B slightly missed consensus ($31.22B). EPS $2.02 (+29%) includes a $0.11 benefit from tariff refunds. Gross margin 50.1% (includes ~+2pp from tariff refunds; underlying margin is lower). R&D $11.7B (+32%), total operating expenses $19.1B → operating income $35.695B (confirmed in 10-Q: gross margin $54.77B - operating expenses $19.075B). The main driver of the share decline was a conservative Q4 guide citing 'supply constraints': FX headwind of -2.5pp and gross margin of 47–48% (initial reaction to the Services miss -3–4% → widened to -8% after the guidance, varies by source). Tim Cook's last earnings call (successor: John Ternus).

FQ4 guidance: revenue $50B (well above consensus of $43–44B), EPS $31, CapEx about $10B (~$27B for the full FY). Expects the shortage to 'persist beyond 2027'. 2026Q2/NVDA/notes.text: ★Record quarter; fifth straight beat. Revenue $96.2B (+18% QoQ, +106% YoY), +4.5% vs consensus ($92.1B). Data-center revenue $89.0B (+117% YoY, 92.5% of total), driven by the Blackwell Ultra ramp. GAAP operating income $63.7B (+124% YoY), operating margin 66.2% (below Micron's 80.4% and SK hynix's 76.3%). GAAP net income $59.7B (EPS $2.46); non-GAAP EPS $2.22 (+6.3% vs consensus of $2.09). Gross margin 75.0% (72.4% a year earlier). ※Warned in advance that soaring memory prices could push gross margin down to 71–72% in Q4 — a sign that even Nvidia faces cost pressure from the memory shortage. Q3 guidance: revenue $108.0B ±2% (about $3.8B above consensus), gross margin ~74.0%. Supply commitments (mainly memory procurement) jumped from $119B to $279B quarter over quarter. Backlog topped $2T. The CFO expects the top five hyperscalers' CapEx to rise from $800B+ in 2026 to $1.3T in 2027 — consistent with the GOOGL, MSFT, META and AMZN CapEx raises noted above. Announced an expanded AWS partnership (2 million+ GPUs plus new Vera CPUs, partly integrated with next-generation Rubin). Buybacks plus dividends $26.0B (remaining authorization $99.0B); issued $25B of bonds. Shares rose about +5% after hours during the call — in contrast to declines after each of the previous four reports.
